headline: Signs You Need Professional Help for Your Kitchen Backsplash
articleBody:
Tile work seems manageable until you confront uneven walls, intricate patterns, or tricky electrical cuts. Knowing when to hire a licensed general contractor can spare you costly materials and frustration.

Visible Signals It Is Time to Hire a Pro:
- Wavy or bowed drywall: If your wall bows in and out, standard tile sheets will sit unevenly, creating noticeable "lippage" where edges stick out. A contractor levels the backing before setting tile.
- Working with natural stone or fragile glass: Marble, slate, and glass tiles require specialized wet-saw blades and specific setting mortars that will not bleed through or stain porous surfaces.
- Multiple electrical outlets along the run: Precision cutting around four or five dual-gang outlets on a single wall requires diamond tooling and box extenders so switches mount flush and safe.
- Moving or adding power outlets: If your new layout calls for shifting receptacles or adding under-cabinet lighting wires, licensed trade coordination is necessary to satisfy local codes.
- High-moisture or heat zones behind the range: Cooking heat and grease splatter demand heat-tolerant thin-set and properly sealed grout lines that hold up under heavy daily cleaning.

What to Do Next:
Getting straight cuts, even grout joints, and proper perimeter movement joints requires technical skill and the right tools.
